heading: Whole-home water filtration in Asheville, NC
intro: Chlorine taste at the kitchen sink? Orange stains in the tub? Tell us what you’re noticing. We’ll help you work out what to test and which system fits your home.
caption: A Western North Carolina basement installation with three treatment tanks, a brine tank and sediment filtration.

sections.heading: If you have city water
paragraphs: If the taste of chlorine follows you from the kitchen to the shower, whole-home carbon filtration may be a good fit. If the taste is limited to drinking water, a filter at the kitchen sink may be all you need.
Tell us which taps are affected and when you first noticed it. That helps us distinguish a supply issue from a fixture or plumbing issue.

sections.heading: If you have a private well
paragraphs: Grit in a faucet screen, orange staining and a sulfur smell point to different questions. Bring any recent well test and tell us whether the issue affects hot water, cold water or both.
We’ll review the results, the flow your well can sustain and the water your family uses at busy times before recommending treatment stages.

links.label: What to test in well water

sections.heading: What fits in a real home?
paragraphs: In the basement installation pictured here, several tanks sit along one wall. The sediment filter catches particles, and the brine tank supplies salt for the softener. A home that only needs help with chlorine taste may need a much simpler setup.

When we plan a system, we look for room to change a cartridge, refill salt where needed and reach the bypass valve. A photo of where your water line enters the house is useful for the first conversation.

sections.heading: What will a whole-home filter cost?
paragraphs: A quote depends on what needs treating, how much water must flow when showers and laundry run together, and what plumbing or drainage the installation requires. Ask for equipment, installation and ongoing filter or media costs separately so you can compare quotes.

sections.heading: What happens after I request a consultation?
paragraphs: We start with your water source, symptoms and any test results you already have. You’ll get a complimentary personalized water quality report and a recommendation. If you choose to go ahead, a licensed North Carolina plumber handles installation.
